about:
New Berlin Plastics was founded in 1975 by William Aukofer and Robert Zeman in New Berlin, Wisconsin. After relocations in 1976 and 1982, the company moved into a 100,000-square-foot facility in 1998 that serves as its headquarters and manufacturing site. In July 2001, Jeffery Held and Mark Siewert acquired the business and have since expanded its capabilities and customer base.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding with a focus on scientific molding practices. Its services span resin selection, design for manufacturability, mold flow analysis, tool design, program management through a proprietary process called LaunchLogic, tool transfers, and material management. Automation is integrated throughout production, and the facility runs over 100 simultaneous customer projects with a reported 98% on-time launch rate. Quality metrics cited include a 99.8% customer acceptance rate and a 2.2% internal scrap rate.

New Berlin Plastics serves OEMs across a range of sectors including automotive and transportation, healthcare and medical devices, electrical utility, power sports, water treatment, building and construction, controls, lawn and garden, industrial equipment, pet care, marine, small engine, and specialty hand and power tools. The company emphasizes start-to-finish project collaboration and value-added engineering support.

The founders and subsequent owners built the business on predictable outcomes and supply-chain reliability. Leadership states that the goal is to be a low-risk partner that delivers parts on time and within budget, backed by scientific process control and a culture of continuous improvement.
